**Continuous 2.24.0**, a community-maintained fork of the Continue VS Code extension. Continuous is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Continue Dev, Inc.

It installs alongside the original extension (its ID is `b1tninja.continuous`), brings your existing `~/.continue` configuration with it, and collects no telemetry. To update from 2.22.0, 2.20.0, 2.18.0, 2.16.3, 2.16.2, 2.16.1, 2.16.0, 2.14.0, 2.12.x, 2.10.x or 2.4.x, install the new `.vsix` the same way, or let the Marketplace update it. Coming from 2.4.1 or earlier, also see [Continued is now Continuous](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/tag/v2.4.2-vscode) in the 2.4.2 notes: the extension ID changed.

## Install

1. Download the `.vsix` for your platform below and, optionally, check it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
2. Run `code --install-extension continuous-<platform>-2.24.0.vsix --force`, or in VS Code use the Extensions view: `...` → **Install from VSIX…**, then reload the window.

Requires VS Code 1.105 or newer. The packages are not code-signed. Full instructions: [install guide](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/docs/continuous-install.md). Continuous is also on the VS Code Marketplace as **Continuous** (`b1tninja.continuous`).

| Platform                    | File                                                                       |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Windows x64 / Arm64         | `continuous-win32-x64-2.24.0.vsix`, `continuous-win32-arm64-2.24.0.vsix`   |
| macOS Apple Silicon / Intel | `continuous-darwin-arm64-2.24.0.vsix`, `continuous-darwin-x64-2.24.0.vsix` |
| Linux x64 / Arm64           | `continuous-linux-x64-2.24.0.vsix`, `continuous-linux-arm64-2.24.0.vsix`   |

Each platform also has an **agents** build, `continuous-<platform>-2.24.0-agents.vsix`. It adds Continuous to VS Code's Agents window through APIs that are still proposed, so it works in VS Code Insiders, or in Stable started with `code --enable-proposed-api b1tninja.continuous`. Without that it works like the normal build. See [VS Code Chat and Agents](https://b1tninja.github.io/continuous/customize/vscode-chat-and-agents).

## The CLI

The terminal agent is attached as `continuous-cli-2.24.0.tgz`. Install it on Node 22 or newer:

```sh
npm i -g https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/download/v2.24.0-vscode/continuous-cli-2.24.0.tgz
```

The package is `@b1tninja/continuous-cli` and the command is `continuous` (`continuous serve` is the headless server; the notes below call it `cn serve` where the docs do). The short command `cn` also works; both run the same program. It reads the same `~/.continuous` configuration as the extension.

## What's new since 2.22.0

This release is about long agent sessions on Bedrock: tool calls that were reported as cut off when they were not, a context overflow that ended a session without saying why, and a Compact now that failed without a word. It also adds Bedrock rules and prices for OpenAI's closed GPT models and xAI's Grok, and sends an attached file once when it is attached again unchanged.

No new host is contacted by the extension or the terminal agent.

### Behaviour changes

- **An attached file or selection is sent once.** When the same file or selection is attached again and has not changed, later copies in the conversation become a short stub that points at the first one, so a long chat no longer pays for the same file several times.
- **A selection is sent as an attachment.** A selection chip is now attached like a file, and the message text carries a pointer to it: `(see <path> lines <a>-<b>, attached)`.
- **Creating a file outside the workspace is refused.** `create_new_file` no longer writes to an absolute path outside the open workspace folders.

### New

- **Bedrock: OpenAI's closed GPT models and Grok.** GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra and Luna, GPT-6 Sol and Luna and GPT-6.1 Sol, and Grok 4.6 and 4.7, get rules from live probes: `stopSequences` are not sent, a request asks for at least 1,024 output tokens (smaller budgets were spent entirely on reasoning), and Grok takes `reasoning_effort` (it cannot turn reasoning off, so off sends `low`).
- **Prices for Bedrock GPT and Grok**, including the 1.1× premium AWS charges for geographic (`us.`, `eu.`, `apac.` …) inference profiles of these models.
- **Session attachments in the context meter.** The meter lists what the session has attached; each row can be opened or removed, and a removal can be undone.

### Fixes

- **False "cut off" on tool calls.** Bedrock stream fragments are matched to their call by `contentBlockIndex`, so parallel tool calls no longer pick up each other's arguments. "Cut off" is shown only when the reply hit its output limit; otherwise the call says "Incomplete arguments". A stream that was replaced stops.
- **Context overflow ("prompt is too long").** The sizes the provider reports are read, the context estimate for that model is corrected, and the error shows the sizes with **Try again** and **New session**.
- **Compact now failed silently.** The error now reaches the chat: "Compacting failed, so the conversation was not changed: …".
- **Edits that were not applied say why.** The edit tool reports the reason (`EditNotAppliedError`) instead of a bare failure.
- **Bedrock Mantle** reuses the request path and quirks it learned, per region and model.

### Docs

- `plans/context-policy.md` and `plans/context-references.md`: how context is kept, compacted and attached, and how other agents do it.

### Upgrade notes

- **Firewalls and sandboxes.** No new host.
- **Bedrock GPT and Grok output budget.** A `maxTokens` below 1,024 for these models is raised to 1,024.
